<reason>B won the proportionality comparison while conceding genuinely private technology and some protective benefit. It distinguished reduced exposure from blocked visits, exclusion from annoyance, and transactional gambling controls from pornography gates. A supplied plausible friction and fallback mechanisms, but overstated their effectiveness and treated the proposition’s intrusion clause as settling the very balance under debate. B answered both pressure questions directly; A repeatedly mischaracterized B’s stronger rationale for gambling as an outright concession and its proposed mandatory defaults as merely opt-in tools.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal exposed the weakness in A’s liquor-cabinet analogy: online substitution can require only another link, not acquiring restricted physical goods. A answered by repeating that exposure starts on mainstream sites; B correctly explained that this does not establish where exposure occurs after gating. That left A’s claimed overwhelming reduction unsupported without requiring perfect enforcement.</best_rebuttal>
